tags.par: creates a team of threads (a parallel region)
tags.ws: worksharing: divides work among the threads of the current team, so it may be orphaned
tags.loop: applies to the loop nest that follows
tags.offload: runs on or moves data to a device (offloading)

fields.c: the leaf constructs of a compound
fields.u: the 6.x spelling with underscores (directive names are keyed with blanks)
fields.s: our own one-line summary (the most used items only)
fields.since: the version that added it, when no contents page lists it
fields.g: the clause group whose section documents it
fields.ty: the type of a named constant
fields.l: link: p holds the page of each version in `versions` order (null: not in that version), f the fragment, fv the fragments that differ by version

legend.keys: directive names are lower case with blanks (target data, declare simd); clauses, routines, kinds and constants lower case; environment variables upper case
legend.constants: the named constants of omp_lib, with their type (ty) and the link of their kind; the allocator-trait keys and values (omp_atk_*, omp_atv_*) and interop runtime IDs (omp_ifr_*) are left out

libgomp.rule: routines and environment variables; _ is written _005f (omp_get_thread_num → omp_005fget_005fthread_005fnum)

allocate.s: Allocates variables with an OpenMP memory allocator.

allocators.s: Allocates the arrays of the following ALLOCATE statement with an OpenMP memory allocator.

barrier.s: Every thread of the team waits here until all have arrived.

cancel.s: Requests the cancellation of the innermost enclosing region of the given type.

cancellation point.s: A point where a thread checks whether cancellation was requested.

critical.s: Only one thread at a time runs the enclosed block (per critical name).

declare mapper.s: Defines how variables of a derived type are mapped to devices.

declare reduction.s: Defines a reduction operator for REDUCTION clauses.

declare simd.s: Declares a procedure callable from vectorised loops, with SIMD versions.

declare target.s: Makes procedures or variables available on devices.

declare variant.s: Declares a specialised version of a procedure for some contexts.

depobj.s: Initialises, updates or destroys a dependence object.

dispatch.s: Calls a procedure variant chosen for the current context.

distribute.s: Divides the iterations of a loop among the teams of a league.

do.s: Divides the iterations of the following DO loop among the threads of the team.

error.s: Reports an error or warning at compile time or at run time.

flush.s: Makes this thread’s view of memory consistent with the other threads’.

interop.s: Creates, uses or destroys interoperability objects for foreign runtimes.

loop.s: Declares that the iterations of a loop may run concurrently; the implementation picks how.

masked.s: The enclosed block runs only on the primary thread (or the threads the FILTER clause selects).

metadirective.s: Chooses one of several directives by the context, at compile time or at run time.

nothing.s: A directive that does nothing (for metadirectives).

ordered.s: Runs the enclosed block in the order of the loop iterations.

parallel.s: Starts a parallel region: a team of threads runs the enclosed block.

requires.s: States the implementation features the program needs.

scan.s: Separates the input and scan phases of a loop with an inclusive or exclusive scan.

scope.s: A block that the whole team runs, with its own data-sharing and reduction clauses.

section.s: One block of work inside a SECTIONS construct.

sections.s: Runs each enclosed SECTION once, on some thread of the team.

simd.s: Vectorises the following loop with SIMD instructions.

single.s: The enclosed block runs on one thread; the others wait at its end unless NOWAIT is given.

target.s: Runs the enclosed block on a device (offloading), mapping the data it uses.

target data.s: Maps variables to a device for the duration of the enclosed block.

target enter data.s: Maps variables to a device until a matching TARGET EXIT DATA.

target exit data.s: Ends the device mapping of variables, copying them back if asked.

target update.s: Copies mapped variables between the host and a device.

task.s: Creates a task: the block may run later, on any thread of the team.

taskgroup.s: Waits at its end for every task created inside it, descendants included.

taskloop.s: Divides the iterations of a loop into tasks.

taskwait.s: Waits for the child tasks of the current task to complete.

taskyield.s: Lets the current task be suspended in favour of other tasks.

teams.s: Starts a league of teams, each with its own initial thread.

threadprivate.s: Gives each thread its own copy of a module or common-block variable.

workshare.s: Divides the array assignments, FORALL and WHERE statements of the block among the threads.

master.s: Deprecated synonym of MASKED: the block runs only on the primary thread.

parallel do.s: Starts a parallel region whose only content is a worksharing DO loop.

parallel do simd.s: A parallel region with a worksharing loop whose chunks are also vectorised.

do simd.s: Divides a loop among the threads and vectorises each thread’s chunk.

parallel sections.s: Starts a parallel region whose only content is a SECTIONS construct.

parallel workshare.s: Starts a parallel region whose only content is a WORKSHARE construct.

parallel loop.s: Starts a parallel region whose only content is a LOOP construct.

taskloop simd.s: Divides a loop into tasks whose iterations are also vectorised.

distribute parallel do.s: Divides a loop among teams, then among the threads of each team.

teams distribute.s: Starts a league of teams and divides a loop among them.

target parallel do.s: Offloads a parallel worksharing loop to a device.

target teams.s: Offloads the block to a device and starts a league of teams there.

target teams distribute parallel do.s: Offloads a loop and spreads it over the teams and threads of a device.

target teams distribute parallel do simd.s: Offloads a loop and spreads it over teams, threads and SIMD lanes of a device.

target teams loop.s: Offloads a loop and lets the implementation spread it over the device.

affinity.s: A hint to run the task close to the listed data.

aligned.s: Declares the alignment of the listed arrays or pointers.

allocate.s: Allocates the private copies with an OpenMP memory allocator.

bind.s: What a LOOP construct binds to: teams, parallel or thread.

capture.s: An atomic update that also captures the old or new value.

collapse.s: Applies the construct to the given number of nested loops, as one iteration space.

collector.s: The collector of an induction (DECLARE INDUCTION).

copyin.s: Copies the primary thread’s threadprivate values to the other threads.

copyprivate.s: Broadcasts a value from the thread that ran a SINGLE to the others.

default.s: Sets the data-sharing attribute of variables not listed in any clause.

defaultmap.s: The default mapping of variables of a given kind.

depend.s: Orders tasks by their dependences on variables (in, out, inout, …).

detach.s: The task completes only when its event is fulfilled.

device.s: The device the construct runs on.

device_type.s: Which devices a DECLARE TARGET applies to: host, nohost or any.

dist_schedule.s: How loop iterations are divided among teams.

enter.s: Makes variables or procedures available on devices (DECLARE TARGET).

filter.s: The thread that runs a MASKED region.

final.s: If true, the task’s descendant tasks run immediately, undeferred.

firstprivate.s: Each thread gets its own copy, initialised from the original variable.

from.s: Copies variables from a device (TARGET UPDATE).

grainsize.s: The number of loop iterations per task.

has_device_addr.s: The listed variables already have device addresses.

hint.s: A hint for a CRITICAL or ATOMIC construct (contended, speculative, …).

if.s: Runs the construct (in parallel, or offloaded) only if the condition is true.

in_reduction.s: The task takes part in a task reduction.

is_device_ptr.s: The listed pointers already hold device addresses.

lastprivate.s: Private copies, with the value from the last iteration or section copied back.

linear.s: Private variables whose value is a linear function of the loop iteration.

link.s: Maps a variable to devices only when a region uses it (DECLARE TARGET).

map.s: Maps variables between the host and a device: to, from, tofrom, alloc, release or delete.

mergeable.s: The task may share the data environment of its parent.

nogroup.s: A TASKLOOP without its implied TASKGROUP.

nontemporal.s: The listed variables are accessed without temporal locality.

nowait.s: Removes the implied barrier at the end of the construct.

num_tasks.s: The number of tasks a TASKLOOP creates.

num_teams.s: The number of teams in the league.

num_threads.s: The number of threads of the parallel region.

order.s: order(concurrent): the iterations may run in any order, or concurrently.

ordered.s: The loop has ordered regions (or, with an argument, doacross dependences).

priority.s: A hint of the task’s priority.

private.s: Each thread gets its own, uninitialised copy of the listed variables.

proc_bind.s: How the threads are placed on the hardware: primary, close or spread.

reduction.s: Combines each thread’s private copy with an operator (+, max, …) at the end.

safelen.s: The largest distance between iterations that may run concurrently in SIMD.

schedule.s: How loop iterations are divided among threads: static, dynamic, guided, auto or runtime.

shared.s: All threads use the original variables.

simdlen.s: The preferred number of iterations to run concurrently in SIMD.

task_reduction.s: Starts a reduction that the tasks of a TASKGROUP take part in.

thread_limit.s: The largest number of threads per team.

to.s: Copies variables to a device (TARGET UPDATE), or declares them on devices.

untied.s: A suspended task may resume on another thread.

update.s: An atomic update (the default for ATOMIC).

use_device_addr.s: In the region, the listed variables refer to their device copies.

use_device_ptr.s: In the region, the listed pointers hold device addresses.

omp_alloc.s: Allocates memory with an OpenMP allocator.

omp_display_affinity.s: Prints the thread-affinity information of the calling thread.

omp_display_env.s: Prints the OpenMP version and settings.

omp_free.s: Frees memory allocated with an OpenMP allocator.

omp_fulfill_event.s: Fulfils the event of a detached task.

omp_get_active_level.s: Returns the number of nested active parallel regions enclosing the call.

omp_get_ancestor_thread_num.s: Returns the thread number of the calling thread’s ancestor at a nesting level.

omp_get_default_device.s: Returns the default device for target regions.

omp_get_device_num.s: Returns the device the calling thread runs on.

omp_get_dynamic.s: Returns whether the runtime may adjust the number of threads.

omp_get_initial_device.s: Returns the device number of the host.

omp_get_level.s: Returns the number of nested parallel regions enclosing the call.

omp_get_mapped_ptr.s: Returns the device address of a mapped host address.

omp_get_max_active_levels.s: Returns the deepest nesting of active parallel regions allowed.

omp_get_max_task_priority.s: Returns the largest task priority allowed.

omp_get_max_teams.s: Returns the most teams a TEAMS construct without NUM_TEAMS would get.

omp_get_max_threads.s: Returns the most threads a parallel region without NUM_THREADS would get.

omp_get_nested.s: Deprecated: returns whether nested parallelism is enabled.

omp_get_num_devices.s: Returns the number of non-host devices.

omp_get_num_places.s: Returns the number of places available.

omp_get_num_procs.s: Returns the number of processors available to the program.

omp_get_num_teams.s: Returns the number of teams in the league.

omp_get_num_threads.s: Returns the number of threads in the current team.

omp_get_place_num.s: Returns the place the calling thread is bound to.

omp_get_proc_bind.s: Returns the thread-affinity policy of the next parallel region.

omp_get_schedule.s: Returns the schedule of loops with schedule(runtime).

omp_get_team_num.s: Returns the number of the calling thread’s team, from 0.

omp_get_team_size.s: Returns the size of the team at a nesting level.

omp_get_thread_limit.s: Returns the largest number of threads available to the program.

omp_get_thread_num.s: Returns the number of the calling thread in its team, from 0.

omp_get_wtick.s: Returns the resolution of omp_get_wtime, in seconds.

omp_get_wtime.s: Returns the elapsed wall-clock time, in seconds.

omp_in_parallel.s: Returns .true. inside an active parallel region.

omp_init_allocator.s: Creates a memory allocator with the given traits.

omp_pause_resource.s: Frees the resources the runtime holds on a device.

omp_pause_resource_all.s: Frees the resources the runtime holds on every device.

omp_set_default_device.s: Sets the default device for target regions.

omp_set_dynamic.s: Lets the runtime adjust the number of threads of parallel regions, or stops it.

omp_set_lock.s: Waits for a simple lock and acquires it.

omp_set_max_active_levels.s: Sets the deepest nesting of active parallel regions.

omp_set_nest_lock.s: Acquires a nestable lock, which its owner may acquire again.

omp_set_nested.s: Deprecated: enables nested parallelism; use omp_set_max_active_levels.

omp_set_num_teams.s: Sets the number of teams for later TEAMS constructs.

omp_set_num_threads.s: Sets the number of threads for later parallel regions.

omp_set_schedule.s: Sets the schedule of loops with schedule(runtime).

omp_target_associate_ptr.s: Associates a host address with device memory.

omp_target_disassociate_ptr.s: Removes the association of a host address with device memory.

omp_target_is_present.s: Returns whether a host address has a device copy.

omp_target_memcpy.s: Copies memory between host and device, or between devices.

omp_test_lock.s: Acquires a simple lock if it is free, without waiting; returns whether it did.

omp_test_nest_lock.s: Acquires a nestable lock if it is free or owned; returns the nesting count.

OMP_DEFAULT_DEVICE.s: The default device for target regions.

OMP_DISPLAY_AFFINITY.s: Prints each thread’s affinity when it changes.

OMP_DISPLAY_ENV.s: Prints the OpenMP version and settings at start-up.

OMP_DYNAMIC.s: Whether the runtime may adjust the number of threads.

OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS.s: The deepest nesting of active parallel regions.

OMP_NESTED.s: Deprecated: enables nested parallelism; use OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS.

OMP_NUM_TEAMS.s: The most teams a TEAMS construct may create.

OMP_NUM_THREADS.s: The number of threads of parallel regions, per nesting level.

OMP_PLACES.s: The places threads are bound to: threads, cores, sockets, ll_caches, numa_domains or a list.

OMP_PROC_BIND.s: How threads are bound to places: false, true, primary, close or spread.

OMP_SCHEDULE.s: The schedule of loops with schedule(runtime).

OMP_STACKSIZE.s: The stack size of the threads OpenMP creates.

OMP_TARGET_OFFLOAD.s: Whether offloading is mandatory, disabled or the default.

OMP_THREAD_LIMIT.s: The largest number of threads the program may use.

OMP_TOOL.s: Whether a tool (OMPT) may be loaded.

OMP_WAIT_POLICY.s: Whether waiting threads spin (active) or sleep (passive).
